transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really extreme and exhausting mood swings over the past several months. Sometimes I feel this intense, overflowing energy where I'm incredibly high or easily irritated, but then I crash into phases of deep sadness and emptiness. It's just gotten to be too much to handle on my own.

During your high or low mood periods, have you ever had hallucinations or fixed beliefs that seemed out of touch with reality, and if so, have those symptoms ever lasted for at least two weeks when your mood was otherwise normal?

Yes, I have definitely experienced some strange beliefs and heard things that others couldn't, but that only ever happens when my mood is extremely high and energetic. Those experiences completely go away when my mood settles down, so they have never happened or lasted when my mood was normal.

Have you ever had a period of at least one week of abnormally elevated or irritable mood with much more energy, where you needed much less sleep or did things that caused major problems, hospitalization, or were clearly out of character?

Yes, I absolutely have. I went through a phase where I felt abnormally happy and bursting with energy, but at the same time, I was extremely irritable and would snap over the smallest things. This state actually lasted for about five months, which was way longer than just a week.

When you had those hallucinations or strange beliefs, were they present only during the mood episodes, or did they ever continue for at least two weeks after the mood symptoms had gone back to normal?

They only happened during those times when I was feeling extremely high-energy and hyperactive. Once those intense mood episodes ended, the hallucinations and strange beliefs completely stopped as well. They never continued on their own when my mood went back to normal.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features]. The patient reports clear manic episodes lasting about five months, which supports Bipolar I Disorder. Although there were hallucinations and strange beliefs, they occurred only during the manic/high-energy mood episodes and never persisted for at least two weeks when mood was normal, which argues against Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features as a separate diagnosis in this framework. Therefore the current candidate list is narrowed to Bipolar I Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: History is most consistent with a manic episode lasting months with markedly elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and psychotic symptoms (hallucinations/delusional beliefs) occurring only during mood episodes and resolving when mood normalizes. There is no evidence of psychosis persisting for 2 weeks outside mood symptoms, which argues against schizoaffective disorder.
